articles.title: Trump says he’s creating an AI force and appointing a czar amid concerns over the rapidly developing tech
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced Saturday that he will appoint a czar to take point on artificial intelligence and will also create an AI task force.
articles.body: President Donald Trump announced Saturday that he will appoint a czar to take point on artificial intelligence and will also create an AI task force. The move comes after AI researchers warned that the technology could soon spiral out of human control, sparking concerns and calls for industry regulation. Trump said in a social media post Saturday he would not let the “decimation” of AI happen. “We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System. For this purpose, I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force,” Trump said on Truth Social. Trump added that “only High I.Q. individuals need apply” to the new AI czar role, to which he did not name an appointee in the post. Trump has seemed unfazed by the warnings over the last two weeks, calling them a “hoax” and saying the priority should be for the U.S. to lead in AI development and beat China. “Whoever wins AI wins,” Trump said multiple times over the last week. In a flurry of social media posts, the president launched a full-throated defense of the technology, and he even called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while Huang was onstage at an industry summit to talk about the issue. The White House did not immediately provide more details on Trump’s new initiative. While lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have attempted to advance legislation in the past few years, it has not gone anywhere. But members of Congress are once again discussing the issue amid renewed warnings. During a closed-door briefing on the topic this week, Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, known as the “godfather of AI,” warned lawmakers that time was running out to regulate the industry, telling them Congress has “maybe a year” to get the job done. Trump previously had an AI and cryptocurrency czar, David Sacks, who stepped down earlier this year due to limits on his term as a special government employee. Sacks has since taken an advisory role in the administration and is expected to join Trump’s state dinner with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Democrats widely seen as 2028 presidential hopefuls have made moves to regulate AI at the state level. California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on Friday seeking to increase oversight of the industry and urged a task force to consider requiring the creation of a kill switch. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro has called on the federal government to regulate AI, and Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger launched an AI task force and data center accountability plan aimed at addressing “growing concern and risks posed by the rapid development of artificial intelligence.” Former President Barack Obama advised Democrats during an fundraiser last week to prioritize creating a plan on the issue and said he would make it a central issue if he were running in 2028.

articles.title: Hasan Piker says he’d ‘absolutely’ campaign for AOC in 2028 as El-Sayed distances himself
articles.summary: Hasan Piker told Axios he'd "absolutely" campaign for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in 2028, revealing contacts with Bernie Sanders and other liberals
articles.body: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker said he would "absolutely" campaign for Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., if she runs for president in 2028, as some Democratic politicians distance themselves from the streamer over his past remarks. Appearing on an episode of "The Axios Show," taped in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Piker revealed his interest in working as a campaign surrogate for Ocasio-Cortez. "What goes on behind the scenes in the Democratic Party and what gets talked about is entirely different, I think in many respects," Piker said. Asked point-blank if he would campaign for Ocasio-Cortez in 2028, Piker said, "Oh, absolutely, yes." HASAN PIKER MAKES AOC HIS 2028 PICK FOR PRESIDENT, SAYS IT'S 'NOT EVEN A QUESTION’ The controversial streamer revealed he has also been in touch with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-VT, along with "politicians that you would not expect, that are not immediately seen as allies to Democratic socialists." Piker's comments come as some Democratic politicians have begun distancing themselves from him following controversial remarks — including Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic U.S. Senate nominee in Michigan. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES When asked if Piker had been invited to campaign for El-Sayed, he said that he had not been asked to stay away from — or come to — Michigan. "If my services are needed, I’ll go wherever," Piker said. HASAN PIKER INSISTS ABDUL EL-SAYED ASKED HIM TO 'STUMP' FOR MICHIGAN CAMPAIGN AMID BACKLASH He added that if El-Sayed were to call on him to campaign this close to the upcoming midterms, "there’d be real deep problems." "My job isn’t to get 65-plus-year-olds out to vote for the Democratic candidate," Piker continued. "My job is to get under 45-year-old, college-educated, and non-college-educated men to come out and participate." LIZ PEEK: HASAN PIKER EXPOSES DEMOCRATS' DESPERATION TO WIN BACK YOUNG MEN Piker's comments during the Axios interview drew a public rebuke from El-Sayed after interviewer Alex Thompson recalled Piker's previous statement that "America is the top dog in terrorism." "Do you think America, then, is worse than al Qaeda?" Thompson asked. RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORIST COMPARISON "Pound for pound as far as the number of deaths, yes," Piker replied. "We have caused tremendous terror all around the world." "I think that that is not only terror that we are waging on regular civilians, and nations in the periphery, but it's also having consequences on ourselves," the Twitch streamer continued. "It's having dramatic consequences on the home front." RASKIN CALLS PIKER’S RHETORIC 'IRRELEVANT DISTRACTION' AFTER THE STREAMER SAID HE'D VOTE FOR HAMAS OVER ISRAEL "One clear example of this is what we did in Minab [Iran]," Piker said, referring to a strike on a school earlier this year. A United Nations fact-finding mission said it found "reasonable grounds to believe" the U.S. carried out the strike and that the attack amounted to the war crime of launching an indiscriminate attack. "There's no distinction between blowing up a school, triple-tapping it with Tomahawk missiles. If you're killing 140 schoolgirls, that is an act of terror." WATCH: Hasan Piker says he would campaign for AOC if she runs for president Piker finished his thought by conceding that not all Americans are terrorists, but emphasized the need for an "environment of accountability." ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM The Twitch streamer’s inflammatory stance was quickly denounced by El-Sayed’s campaign, which condemned the views in a statement to Axios and Fox News Digital. "I do not agree with this statement [on al-Qaeda], nor do I give much weight to the statements made by a social media streamer," the campaign told the outlet. "I am more concerned with the dangerous policies of Donald Trump and Mike Rogers that are raising the prices of gas, groceries and healthcare for Michiganders." FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER CALLED OUT BY MS NOW HOSTS IN FIERY EXCHANGE OVER HIM BEING A DRAG FOR DEMOCRATS Piker’s apparent scramble to align himself with high-profile Democrats ahead of the midterm elections was noted by Kaivan Shroff, a media commentator and former digital organizer for Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign. "The central tension with Hasan is that he wants his electoral influence taken seriously, but he also wants to operate like a streamer with no responsibility for what his comments create for the candidates he supports," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "You can’t claim credit for helping politicians win and then treat the consequences of your own rhetoric as their problem." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Shroff said that Piker’s comments regarding Ocasio-Cortez are "a perfect example," adding that, "saying publicly that you’re talking to her and her team turns that relationship into a political story whether they wanted one or not. If the goal is to help a candidate, sometimes the most useful thing you can do is not make yourself the story." He also pointed to the conflicting priorities between Piker and El-Sayed, which may be a factor in the division between the two far-left Democrats. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "El-Sayed has every reason to make clear that Hasan does not speak for his campaign, and Hasan criticizing him for creating that distance exposes the conflicting incentives here," Shroff said. "A candidate has to answer to voters…a streamer has to keep an audience engaged. If Hasan really wants to help the candidates he supports, an easier solution would be to stop handing them inflammatory comments they then have to explain and go away for a while." Fox News Digital reached out to Piker and representatives for Ocasio-Cortez for comment. Fox News Digital’s Peter D’Abrosca contributed to this report.

articles.body:
President Trump announced plans Saturday to create an “AI Force” as well as appoint a “czar” to oversee the emerging technology’s development.

In a lengthy Truth Social post, Trump called the concerns surrounding a lack of federal AI guardrails a “hoax,” adding he would not allow for the technology’s “decimation” as its U.S.-based industry leaders compete with other countries — namely China.

“We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System,” he wrote on Truth Social.

The president compared his proposed “AI Force” to the Space Force, which he established during his first term, but did not elaborate on how the agency would operate or what its duties would entail.

For the new “AI Czar” position, Trump said, “Only High I.Q. individuals need to apply!” He did not expand further on the latest iteration of the role.

Trump previously had an AI and cryptocurrency czar, venture capitalist David Sacks, a special government employee who held the post before stepping down earlier this year.

The announcement comes as AI researchers, tech CEOs and global leaders warn about the need for safeguards as the industry develops increasingly powerful AI systems.

For example, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a global slowdown, which was met with agreement from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk, of SpaceX, SpaceXAI and Tesla.

Trump has resisted calls for new federal restrictions, arguing that slowing the industry could threaten the U.S.’s global position in the AI race. His administration has instead emphasized accelerating the emerging technology’s development while using guidelines to address potential issues.

“We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry,” Trump wrote Saturday. “Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows!”
